newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Hang Seng closes above 12,000 points.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Hang Seng closes above 12,000 points.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng index powered through the 12,000 point level on Thursday, closing above that mark for the first time since February 1994, buoyed by local fundamentals and record highs in overseas markets.
The Hang Seng closed up 62.68 points at 12,014.56. Turnover was HK$7.85 billion compared to Wednesday's HK$6.26 billion.

"The market seems to be very strong, particularly today. I think it is due to overseas markets which are right now at peaks," said Edwin Cheung, dealing director at Taiwan Securities. "Corporate earnings are contributing to this rally."
The blue-chip index hit a 1996 intra-day high at 12,022.38 during Thursday's session.
"It has broken out again. You just can't keep this market down," said Howard Gorges, director at South China Brokerage.
"It seems to want to push up to the next resistance which is 12,100 to 12,200," he said.
The last time the Hang Seng index traded above the 12,000 point level was on February 4, 1994. It hit an intra-day high of 12,186.80 on that day before closing at 12,157.57.
"That's the number that people had been awaiting for a couple of years now and we did it today," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
Analysts said Hong Kong stocks could run into some profit-taking now after seven straight winning sessions during which the index has advanced 468 points.
"It could run into profit-taking any time but I don't think it will be damaging to the market, just healthy," said Gorges.
Frederick Tsang, head of research at PrimeEast Securities, said investors may choose to focus on laggards which may not fall as much as market leaders during a bout of profit-taking.
HSBC Holdings rose HK$2.00 to HK$146.00 after hitting an all-time high during the session of HK$146.50.
"We have good leadership in the market again," said Gorges.
Red chips were also well bid with CITIC Pacific up HK$0.90 at HK$36.00 and Guangdong Investment up HK$0.10 at HK$5.80.

Sun Hung Kai Properties fell HK$0.25 to HK$81.50. It posted 1995/96 net profit of HK$11.04 billion compared to HK$10.36 billion. Henderson Land rose HK$0.75 to HK$66.75, after hitting a record intra-day high during the session at HK$67.00.

"There is quite a bit of buying interest for Henderson Land. There is probably some switching out of Sun Hung Kai Properties into Henderson Land - the dividend is better and the PE lower," said Tsang.
